subject: Discovery recap: migration off proprietary LLM APIs -> open models (Acme Corp)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Nguyen <sarah.nguyen@acme.com>; Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@acme.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 22 Mar 2026 15:15:00 -0700
Subject: Discovery recap: migration off proprietary LLM APIs -> open models (Acme Corp)

Hi Sarah / Tom 

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap from our discovery to make sure we captured the right priorities and next steps. Please reply with anything I missed or that you'd like spelled out differently.

Pain points you described
- High and volatile token costs with current OpenAI usage (completions + embeddings) month-to-month surprises.
- Vendor lock-in concerns: Anthropic/OpenAI-specific SDKs and tooling make it hard to test alternative backends.
- Operational issues: latency spikes for peak inference, lack of reliable per-route SLAs, and limited observability into per-request cost.
- Safety/workflow: you use Anthropic for chain-of-thought safety filtering in some flows worried about preserving similar safety characteristics when switching models.

Current stack we discussed
- Frontend product: chat + assisted search + reranking pipelines.
- OpenAI: chat completions (gpt-4.*) for conversation UI and text-generation; embeddings (text-embedding-3-small) for semantic search.
- Anthropic: used for some safety-sensitive moderation/filtering flows via a separate service.
- Hosting: backend on AWS, some services in us-west-2; keys in your KMS account.

Success criteria for migration / PoC (what matters to you)
- Compatibility: drop-in API compatibility or clear adapter path so minimal engineering effort.
- Quality parity: parity with current completions + embeddings for top 10 customer prompts (you said ~250 seed prompts).
- Cost: target ~40% reduction in per-token/embedding unit cost at target QPS.
- Latency/SLOs: <200ms p95 for single-turn completion paths, predictable scaling for peak.
- Security & compliance: support for KMS/HSM, audit logs, and SOC2 evidence (you requested an initial security doc).

Model shortlist we suggested (initial candidates)
- Llama 2 / Falcon / Mistral family (for chat/completions)
- Mistral Instruct / Llama 2 Chat variants for instruction-following parity
- Open embeddings candidates: Mistral / Cohere open variants or RedPajama embeddings-equivalent

Technical compatibility notes
- Tool + function calling: we recommended testing tool-calling behaviour in a PoC; Redwood provides function-calling shim + fallback policies for models that don't natively support the same interface.
- Quantization/throughput: we can recommend quantized variants to meet latency/cost targets.

Agreed next steps
1) We (Redwood) will produce a PoC scope doc and migration checklist (attached) and a suggested model shortlist + perf estimations.
2) Acme to share: a small seed dataset (~250 prompts + expected outputs), a sample call flow (chat & embedding calls), and any compliance questions to prioritize.
3) Schedule: target 3-week PoC starting mid-April if timelines align.
4) We'll share our SOC2 + security profile and a suggested CAN (cost analysis) for expected QPS.

Attachments: redwood-migration-checklist.xlsx (PoC scope & checklist), redwood-poc-template.docx (PoC kickoff template)

If that all looks right, I can send a formal PoC scope and calendar invite for a kickoff.

Best,
Marissa

From: Sarah Nguyen <sarah.nguyen@acme.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@acme.com>
Date: Mon, 22 Mar 2026 16:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Discovery recap: migration off proprietary LLM APIs -> open models (Acme Corp)

Thanks Marissa  this is great and captures the discussion well. A few clarifications / additions from our side: 

- On usage: our largest cost bucket is embeddings for search + reranking; completions are material but embeddings dominate spend. Monthly spend is around $48k across OpenAI + Anthropic today.
- On safety: Anthropic is used not because it is cheaper but because certain moderation flows hit safety/regulatory requirements; we need to validate that switching models won't regress those checks. If Redwood can help with a safety/evals plan that'd be ideal.
- API compatibility: we call OpenAI's ChatCompletion API today and use tool-calling via a custom proxy. We'd prefer a migration path that doesn't require rewriting our entire backend SDK.
- Fine-tuning vs instruction-tuning: we don't plan to fine-tune models now but need to support instruction-tuned variants and eventual adapters.

We can share the 250-seed prompt set (sanitized) and a sample of the embedding vectors pipeline by EOD Wednesday.

Questions for Redwood: can you include expected p75/p95 latency estimates and a model-cost estimate for the shortlist you recommended? Also, what metrics do you suggest collecting during the PoC to prove quality parity?

Happy to kick off the PoC  Tom and I prefer a mid-April start (week of Apr 12).

 Sarah
Lead PM, AI Platform | Acme Corp
sarah.nguyen@acme.com | +1 (206) 555-0199

Thanks Sarah  helpful notes. Quick answers inline and next steps below.

- Embeddings focus: noted. We'll prioritize embedding-cost and latency estimates in the PoC and include a reranking-quality evaluation (MRR + recall@k) on your seed prompts.
- Safety/evals: we'll include a safety evaluation plan and run your moderation flows against candidate models; we'll provide suggested thresholds and a remediation checklist.
- API adapter: Redwood can act as a drop-in routing layer (same route names) and provide SDK shims so your backend calls the same functions. For tool-calling we'll validate the proxy approach in week 1 of the PoC.
- Latency/cost estimates: we'll include p50/p75/p95 estimates for completion and embedding flows for each model variant in the PoC doc.

Action items I own (by Fri, Mar 26):
- PoC scope + model shortlist + estimated latency/cost per model (doc + pricing CAN).
- Security profile and SOC2 summary (we'll attach the standard packet).

Action items for Acme (by Wed, Mar 24):
- Share seed prompt set and embedding pipeline sample + expected traffic profile (QPS).

Proposed PoC kickoff: Apr 13 (Tue) 10:00am PT  I will send a calendar invite once we confirm.

Attachments: redwood-migration-checklist.xlsx, redwood-poc-template.docx

Best,
Marissa
